extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers (and institutional representatives) applying to NIA K99/R00 awards in aging research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, and transitioning a K99/R00 Pathway to Independence application to NIA, including eligibility rules, application contents, timing, budget limits, and the R00 faculty-position requirements. Also addresses visa documentation, eligibility-window extensions, and human/animal research approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99 eligibility — postdoctoral experience limit
rubrics_metrics.description: K99 applicants must be in mentored, non-independent research positions, working in the U.S., with no more than four years of research experience after Ph.D. conferral at the time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time spent conducting research in your Ph.D. lab after receiving your Ph.D. counts as postdoctoral research experience. Applicants may have no more than four years of postdoctoral research experience by the application due date, regardless of whether they submit a new application or a resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible citizenship/visa status
rubrics_metrics.description: The parent K99/R00 award is open to postdocs conducting research in the United States who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or on a valid U.S. visa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applicants on temporary visas the applicant institution must determine and document in the K99 application that the candidate’s visa will allow them to remain in the U.S. long enough to complete the K99; for the R00 phase the R00 institution must document that the PI's visa will allow them to remain in the U.S. for the R00 award duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/evidence of mentored non-independent position
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for a K99, you must be in a mentored, non-independent research position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your position title does not clearly identify you as postdoc, you must provide evidence that your position is a mentored, non-independent research training position. An official institutional document that includes a description of the position is typically sufficient. A clinical faculty member who does not hold an independent research faculty position may be eligible and should contact NIATraining@mail.nih.gov for guidance. See section III.1 of the parent K99 funding announcement for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility window extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIA will approve requests for extension of the K99 eligibility window for applicants in aging and Alzheimer's/dementia fields both on a regular and case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular approval: one year extension for childbirth within the K99 eligibility window (include child’s date of birth). Case-by-case: parental, medical, or other well-justified leave; disability; extended clinical training; natural disasters; active duty military service. Part-time postdoctoral research training related to personal or family situations or occurring during a research residency or fellowship will be pro-rated accordingly. Extensions for COVID-19 related lab shutdowns or research delays are no longer available. To request an extension or confirm eligibility timeline, email NIATraining@mail.nih.gov no later than 12 weeks before submitting an application and include exact Ph.D. conferral date, start date of your first full-time postdoctoral research position, and a brief summary of research to verify relevance to NIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application due dates and review cycle timing
rubrics_metrics.description: New application due dates: February 12, June 12, October 12; corresponding resubmission and review dates outlined in the NIH career development award cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the NIH Career Development Award Cycle for resubmission and review timing. Consult the notice of funding opportunity and SF 424 (R&R) Application Guide for detailed instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99 and R00 award duration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: K99 (postdoctoral) phase: one to two years. R00 (independent) phase: up to three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan the K99 mentored period to accomplish work that will enable launch of an independent program and to set up the R00 phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget caps and permitted budget components
rubrics_metrics.description: K99 salary up to $75,000 plus fringe; K99 research and career development funds up to $25,000; R00 total budget up to $249,000 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K99 phase yearly award budgets are composed of salary, fringe benefits, research and career development funds, and sometimes travel. R00 yearly award budget covers salary, fringe benefits, research costs, and indirect costs. Additional details are in each award’s notice of funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application narrative content — describe both phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe BOTH the K99 postdoctoral phase and the R00 independent phase of research within the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative should describe what you will accomplish during the mentored phase that will enable you to launch an independent research program (i.e., what you still need to accomplish during the mentored phase in order to compete successfully once independence is achieved). Include a detailed plan for the R00 phase and a clear vision for the research plan of your independent lab; demonstrate ability to articulate a long-term research plan and note that R00 plans may change and will be updated when applying for the R00 transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory committee and mentor documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble an advisory committee including the primary mentor plus two or more co-mentors or advisors and provide letters of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details such as how often and in what format you will meet with mentors and advisors. One individual should be clearly designated as the primary mentor. Include a final evaluation statement by the K99 phase mentor in the R00 application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly describe transition to independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain which aspects of the research are yours to take with you as you establish a lab, and which will remain with your postdoctoral advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants remaining at the K99 institution should provide a plan by which they will separate from their postdoctoral mentor and advance to independence. NIA strongly recommends consulting with your K99 program officer once you have a job offer to ensure it meets R00 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: R00 faculty position eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To transition to the R00 phase, the candidate must have been offered and accepted an assistant professor position that meets specified requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position must be tenure-track, full-time assistant professor (or equivalent only if the department/institution never hires incoming assistant professors on the tenure track; provide evidence such as faculty handbook). Must provide protected research time for duration of R00: minimum of 9 months or 75% research time. Teaching, clinical, and other non-research duties should be minimal. Salary and start-up package must be equivalent to recent new hires (the R00 may not be used to offset start-up package or institutional salary commitment). Appointment may not be contingent on transfer of the R00 award. The institution must support the R00 grantee in applying for independent research funding (e.g., R01).

rubrics_metrics.name: R00 transition application timing and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: R00 transition applications should be submitted 2–4 months before the desired R00 start date; applications must be received no later than 2 months prior to proposed R00 activation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to processing delays at fiscal year end, R00 transition applications with proposed start dates between August 1 and September 30 must be received by June 1 to ensure no interruption in funding. Consult timeline table: desired R00 start date November 1–July 31 => at least 2 months prior; August 1–September 30 => by June 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: R00 application submission method and required institutional roles
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent phase institution must submit an application on behalf of the candidate for the R00 Award using the PHS 398 Application. The R00 institution's Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) must submit via the NIA Career Transitions Platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIA guidance also notes the R00 institution's AOR must email the application in PDF format to the program official and the grants specialist on the award and to copy NIATraining@mail.nih.gov to avoid delays. For questions contact NIATraining@mail.nih.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: R00 application required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The R00 application must include a set list of documents and updated materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items include: a new face page signed by the R00 phase institutional representative; a new project description page (update project summary/abstract for R00 plans); detailed non-modular budget pages; updated biographical sketches (PI, collaborators, consultants); a new Resources page; Final Progress Report for the K99 phase; an updated research plan (specific aims updated and research plan briefly described in less than 5 pages); Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan; an updated Bibliography & References Cited; an updated PHS 398 checklist; an offer letter; a letter from the R00 Department/Division Chair describing the institution's commitment to the candidate and plans for career development; a final evaluation statement by the K99 phase mentor. If applicable, include visa documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects and vertebrate animals requirements for R00
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed R00 research involves human subjects or vertebrate animals, updated sections and approvals must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human Subjects: provide an updated Human Subjects section including an 'Inclusion Enrollment Report' and current IRB approval or expected approval date (award not made until final IRB approval granted). Vertebrate Animals: provide an updated Vertebrate Animals section (IACUC approval is Just-In-Time information) and award is not made until final IACUC approval is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research topic appropriateness and pre-submission feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if your K99/R00 research topic is appropriate for NIA and seek feedback if desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the list of currently funded K99/R00 awards. To get feedback on appropriateness, share a one-page overview of specific aims to NIATraining@mail.nih.gov; a scientific program official from the appropriate division will follow up.
